title: Convex and Non-Convex Polygons Assessment
description: Show that you can classify polygons and justify your answer using angles and diagonals.

questions.question: Which condition guarantees that a polygon is convex?
options: It has exactly one diagonal.
All its interior angles are less than 180 degrees.
It has at least one angle greater than 180 degrees.
It has unequal side lengths.
questions.explanation: A polygon is convex when every interior angle is less than 180 degrees.

questions.question: A pentagon has interior angles 85 degrees, 95 degrees, 110 degrees, 250 degrees, and 180 degrees in a rough sketch. Which classification is supported by the 250-degree angle?
options: Convex
Non-convex
Equiangular
Regular
questions.explanation: The 250-degree angle is greater than 180 degrees, so it supports a non-convex classification.

questions.question: A polygon with one inward dent can still be convex if it has many sides.
questions.explanation: Any inward dent makes the polygon non-convex, no matter how many sides it has.

questions.question: Which observation is the best diagonal-based evidence that a polygon is non-convex?
options: One diagonal connects two non-adjacent vertices.
One diagonal lies outside the polygon for part of its length.
The polygon has several diagonals.
The diagonals have different lengths.
questions.explanation: For a non-convex polygon, at least one diagonal goes outside the polygon.

questions.question: A quadrilateral has interior angles 70 degrees, 110 degrees, 80 degrees, and 100 degrees. How should it be classified by convexity?
options: Convex
Non-convex
Not a polygon
Cannot be classified because the sides are unknown
questions.explanation: All four interior angles are less than 180 degrees, so the quadrilateral is convex.

questions.question: A polygon with at least one interior angle greater than 180 degrees is called ____.
questions.explanation: The term is non-convex. It is also sometimes called concave.

questions.question: Explain why side count alone cannot tell whether a hexagon is convex or non-convex.
questions.correctAnswer: Side count alone is not enough because a hexagon can have no inward dents and be convex, or it can have an inward dent and be non-convex.
questions.explanation: Convexity depends on shape behavior, interior angles, and diagonals, not only the number of sides.

questions.question: A student says, 'This polygon is convex because it has all straight sides.' What is the best correction?
options: Straight sides only show that it may be a polygon; convexity depends on inward dents, angles, or diagonals.
Straight sides prove the shape is regular.
Straight sides prove the shape is non-convex.
Only curved sides can form polygons.
questions.explanation: Having straight sides is part of being a polygon, but it does not prove convexity.

questions.question: A diagonal from vertex B to vertex E of a polygon passes outside the shape. Classify the polygon and justify your answer.
questions.correctAnswer: The polygon is non-convex because at least one diagonal passes outside the polygon.
questions.explanation: The diagonal test gives direct evidence: convex polygons keep all diagonals inside.

questions.question: Which pair of statements correctly compares convex and non-convex polygons?
options: Convex polygons have an inward dent; non-convex polygons do not.
Convex polygons keep all diagonals inside; non-convex polygons have at least one diagonal outside.
Convex polygons must be regular; non-convex polygons must be irregular.
Convex polygons have curved sides; non-convex polygons have straight sides.
questions.explanation: The diagonal comparison is correct and is a reliable way to justify the classification.
